requirement_text.REQ-422:
Build-order M3, sequenced immediately after bootstrap on purpose (build-order.md: "Token storage is decided the moment the first token exists"). MOB-5 in docs/mobile/requirements.md, the mobile counterpart of docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md. SECURITY-REVIEWER HARD GATE -- every clause is security content.

BUILDS:
1. Token storage: the lib/auth/ token store REQ-421 created is the only code that touches flutter_secure_storage for tokens, with AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true) and an iOS keychain accessibility of first_unlock_this_device (no iCloud sync). No shared_preferences, file or in-memory-global persistence of a token.
2. Logging: any Dio logging interceptor is either absent or replaced by a redacting one that never emits the Authorization header value, a request/response body of the token endpoint, or a refresh token.
3. Android: AndroidManifest android:usesCleartextTraffic="false" and android:networkSecurityConfig pointing to a main-source-set config whose base-config has cleartextTrafficPermitted="false". DEV-ONLY exception, flagged for SECURITY-REVIEWER: a src/debug/res/xml/ override may permit cleartext for 10.0.2.2 and localhost ONLY. android:allowBackup="false".
3b. App-level transport check: lib/api/api_client.dart refuses any request URL, and bootstrap refuses any tenant-config realm_url, whose scheme is not https in a release build; in debug builds http is allowed for localhost and 10.0.2.2 only.
4. iOS: Info.plist carries no NSAppTransportSecurity exception.
5. Audience scoping: on tenant switch or logout, the previous tenant's tokens are deleted, and a token is only attached to requests for the tenant whose realm issued it.
6. Secret masking: a reusable masked-text widget in lib/design_system/ that masks by default and supports a one-time reveal.
7. [S] items: a "Security hardening before corporate-tier deployment" section in docs/mobile/architecture.md.

result.summary:
Scope test: IN SCOPE — REQ-422/MOB-5 is explicitly a security-content requirement (its own text: 'every clause is security content'); the diff (git diff main...HEAD, 23 files, 3355 insertions) touches secret-resolution code (flutter_secure_storage token store, lib/auth/auth.dart), a lookup/audience-scoping path (iss-check in lib/api/api_client.dart), and transport-security config (AndroidManifest.xml, network_security_config.xml main+debug). Verdicts against the actual diff, read directly (not MOBILE-DEV's summary): INV-1 (tenant data isolation, Ecto :prefix) NOT-APPLICABLE — no Ecto schema/migration/query in this diff; this is a Dart/Flutter mobile-tier change, no backend business-table access. INV-2 (server-side field authorisation) NOT-APPLICABLE — no lib/letflow/routers/ response-shaping code touched; MaskedRevealText is a client-side UX masking widget, not a server authorisation boundary, and does not claim to be one. INV-3 (untrusted runtime sandboxing) NOT-APPLICABLE — no Lua/WASM host-capability code touched. INV-4 (secrets by reference only) APPLIES — this diff resolves/handles secret material (OIDC tokens) end-to-end on-device. Verified: `grep -rln flutter_secure_storage apps/mobile/lib/` returns exactly one file, lib/auth/auth.dart (TenantTokenStore is the sole storage path, matching AC1). `grep -rn 'shared_preferences|dart:io' apps/mobile/lib/auth/ apps/mobile/lib/api/` returns nothing — no plaintext-persistence fallback. `grep -rniE '(password|secret|client_secret|token)\s*(=|:)\s*"[^"]{8,}"' apps/mobile/lib apps/mobile/android` returns nothing — no hardcoded secret literal. Read RedactingLogInterceptor (lib/api/api_client.dart:268-337) directly: onRequest/onResponse/onError all route through _redactHeaders (redacts the Authorization header specifically) and _isTokenEndpoint (fully redacts body for /protocol/openid-connect/token and /oauth2/token paths, matching AC2's threat model) — genuinely functional redaction logic if registered, confirmed by reading the code, not assuming from the name. PASS. INV-5 (not-found/forbidden indistinguishability) NOT-APPLICABLE — no new server lookup-by-ID endpoint in this diff; this is a client. INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) APPLIES as the meta-invariant this handoff itself discharges — satisfied by this handoff's own explicit per-invariant verdicts. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) NOT-APPLICABLE — no SQL, no Repo.query in this diff (Dart/Flutter only). INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) APPLIES — read runTenantBootstrap and switchTenant in lib/bootstrap/navigation_bootstrap.dart in full: every external I/O call (fetchTenantConfig, authenticateWithTenant, tokenStore.store/delete, client.get for memberships/modules) is wrapped in try/catch mapping to a typed BootstrapFailureReason, never a bare pattern match that can raise on tenant-controlled/network input. decodeJwtPayload (lib/auth/auth.dart:239-252) never throws by construction (catches all decode failures, returns null). PASS.

Independent verification of the 3 flagged MINOR issues: (1) flutter_secure_storage AndroidOptions — verified via WebFetch against pub.dev's own changelog and version-11.2.0 docs, not taken on MOBILE-DEV's say-so: v11.0.0's changelog states 'Removed encryptedSharedPreferences parameter from AndroidOptions... The Jetpack Security (EncryptedSharedPreferences) backend is no longer supported' and the v11.2.0 docs confirm the bare AndroidOptions() default now uses AES/GCM/NoPadding data encryption with an Android-Keystore RSA-OAEP-wrapped key — a genuinely different (documented as stronger/modern) mechanism, not a silently-weaker substitute, and the named parameter does not exist under a different name to have been omitted. pubspec.lock confirms the pinned version is exactly 11.2.0. VERDICT: not a blocker — MOBILE-DEV's claim holds up under independent check. (2) switchTenant's extra fetchTenantConfig call — read lib/bootstrap/navigation_bootstrap.dart's switchTenant (lines 279-308) and fetchTenantConfig (lib/api/api_client.dart:343-359) directly. fetchTenantConfig is called via client.getUnauthenticated, which sets options.extra['skipAuth']=true; the bearer interceptor (_bearerInterceptor, api_client.dart:220-240) explicitly checks options.extra['skipAuth']==true and returns before ever reading activeRealm/tokenStore — so this config-fetch request can never carry ANY tenant's token, old or new, closing the leak concern outright. Ordering: previousRealmUrl is deleted (tokenStore.delete + activeRealm.currentRealmUrl=null) strictly before runTenantBootstrap is called; if a request races in the null-activeRealm window, _bearerInterceptor reads realmUrl==null and attaches no Authorization header at all (fails closed, never attaches a stale token) — no window exists where old-tenant-in-new-tenant-context or vice versa can occur. If fetchTenantConfig itself fails, the code defaults to deleting anyway (favors isolation over convenience). VERDICT: not a blocker — no iss-check bypass, no leak window, confirmed by reading the actual interceptor and call-ordering code. (3) tear-off delegation pattern — read the full mechanism (navigation_bootstrap.dart:310-331, 443-479). _switchTenantTopLevel/_logoutTopLevel are tear-offs of the TOP-LEVEL functions, captured at library/module scope (outside any class), which in Dart's scoping rules unambiguously resolves to the top-level declaration (no instance/this receiver exists at module scope to shadow it) — this is exactly the documented Dart resolution-order issue (a bare call inside an instance method of the same name resolves to the instance member first, causing infinite recursion), and the module-scope tear-off is the standard, correct workaround. Critically, these tear-offs capture no TenantTokenStore or any other instance state at all — they are references to stateless top-level functions; every call site passes tokenStore/activeRealm/client as fresh parameters at call time (from `this.tokenStore` etc. inside BootstrapController), so there is no possibility of a stale closure routing a later request to a wrong tenant's token store. VERDICT: not a blocker — benign language-mechanics workaround, confirmed correct by reading the actual capture site and every call site.

Additional independent spot-checks per the dispatch: AndroidManifest.xml (apps/mobile/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml) read directly — usesCleartextTraffic="false", networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config", allowBackup="false", matching AC3/BUILDS-3. Main network_security_config.xml (src/main/res/xml/) read directly — base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false", system trust-anchors only, NO domain-config element (correct per Android's res/xml replace-not-merge semantics — the debug variant fully replaces this file rather than merging). Debug network_security_config.xml (src/debug/res/xml/) read directly — domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true" naming ONLY 10.0.2.2 and localhost (includeSubdomains="false" on both), restating the same false base-config — matches the DEV-ONLY exception scope exactly, no broader cleartext grant. transport_policy.dart read directly — ReleaseTransportPolicy.isUrlAllowed only true for scheme=='https'; DebugTransportPolicy allows https always, http only for host in {10.0.2.2, localhost} (case-insensitive), false otherwise — matches AC5 exactly. Confirmed wired into ApiClient.create's interceptor chain (added before the bearer interceptor, calling handler.reject before handler.next, so no socket opens for a rejected URL) and into runTenantBootstrap's realm_url check (rejects before authenticateWithTenant runs). Audience-scoping/iss-check: _tokenMatchesActiveRealm (api_client.dart:249-252) and issuerOf/decodeJwtPayload (auth.dart:236-261) read directly — fails closed on a determinable iss mismatch, fails open only when iss is undeterminable (matches design's stated OQ-4 resolution), and is invoked inside _bearerInterceptor before any Authorization header is attached. ios/Runner/Info.plist grepped directly for NSAppTransportSecurity/NSAllowsArbitraryLoads — zero matches, confirming the key is genuinely absent (matches AC6, iOS runtime verification correctly stated as DEFERRED). docs/mobile/architecture.md grepped directly — §7 'Security hardening before corporate-tier deployment' present, naming certificate pinning and root/jailbreak detection as [S]-priority, required-before-corporate-tier, not implemented in v1 (matches BUILDS item 7). Token-outside-TenantTokenStore check: repo-wide `grep -rln flutter_secure_storage apps/mobile/lib/` returns only lib/auth/auth.dart — no other file touches the package.

No BLOCKER found on any applicable invariant. All 3 flagged MINOR issues independently verified as genuinely benign (one is a documented strictly-stronger package-version default, one has no actual leak window once the skipAuth/fail-closed mechanics are traced, one is a correct Dart-scoping workaround with no captured instance state) — none is a security-relevant deviation warranting rework.
